sections.intro: The dates Ramtech publishes on its own site.
items: A small modular dealership in Arlington, Texas, in an industry then controlled by large leasing companies.
Frustrated by the product available for complex projects, Ramtech opened its own manufacturing plant on the 20 acre site it still occupies.
The Modular Building Institute awards program starts. Ramtech has since received 31.
Ramtech serves on the Texas Industrial Building Code Council and holds leadership positions with the Modular Building Institute.

sections.heading: Questions we get on the first call
items: Ramtech states that modular construction is usually 25 to 40 percent faster than site construction, because the foundation and the building are made at the same time.
Is modular as durable as site-built?
Ramtech states that modular buildings use the same materials and are built to the same codes as site construction, and last as long when maintained.
What does the no cost planning cover?
A floor plan, a site plan, an exterior rendering, outlined specifications and a preliminary budget, before any design fee.
Can we buy through a purchasing cooperative?
For schools and government agencies, many buildings are available through the cooperatives Ramtech is a vendor for, including BuyBoard and TIPS.
A full one-year written warranty from the date of occupancy on every new building Ramtech manufactures and installs in the continental U.S.

sections.heading: Questions about education
items: Can a school district buy through a cooperative?
For schools and government agencies, many Ramtech relocatable buildings are available through the purchasing cooperatives Ramtech is a vendor for. Ask which cooperative your district belongs to.
Does Ramtech build more than portable classrooms?
Yes. Ramtech builds classroom wings, labs, cafeterias, administrative offices, restroom buildings and complete permanent campuses.
Can the building be moved later?
Relocatable buildings are designed for that. Permanent modular construction is designed to match the life expectancy of a site-built building.

pages.description: Straight answers on modular construction: cost, speed, durability, relocatable versus permanent, purchasing cooperatives, financing and warranty.

sections.heading: Questions, answered plainly.
sections.subhead: Answers drawn from Ramtech's own FAQ. If yours is not here, call or send the form.

sections.heading: About modular construction
items: Ramtech states that modular construction is usually 25 to 40 percent faster than site construction, because the foundation and the building are made at the same time.
Is modular as durable as site-built?
Ramtech states that modular buildings use the same materials and are built to the same codes as site construction, and last as long when maintained.
What does the no cost planning cover?
A floor plan, a site plan, an exterior rendering, outlined specifications and a preliminary budget, before any design fee.
Can we buy through a purchasing cooperative?
For schools and government agencies, many buildings are available through the cooperatives Ramtech is a vendor for, including BuyBoard and TIPS.
A full one-year written warranty from the date of occupancy on every new building Ramtech manufactures and installs in the continental U.S.
Controlled off-site factory production of engineered building sections, typically built 50 to 90 percent complete, then transported to the site, assembled and finished.
What is the difference between relocatable and permanent?

Both are made in the plant with the same materials as site-built structures. Relocatable buildings sit on a concrete block foundation and can be moved. Permanent buildings use a pier and beam or slab-on-grade foundation and site-applied finishes.
Can I finance a modular building?
Ramtech works with third-party finance companies, including finance leases, and can help you compare options.

pitch.heard_intro: What we were given, in your words where we have them. Tell us where it is wrong; your words outrank ours.
heard: The promise a visitor must believe: 'Your building is made in our plant while your site is prepared, so you move in sooner, at a firm fixed price.' It is the first thing on the home page, word for word.
Light ground. Straightforward, professional typography only; no whimsical or quirky display fonts and no heavy black backgrounds. All three directions are light, and the header sits on white.
Showcase is set in Plus Jakarta Sans, as asked.

Design-build leader in commercial modular construction since 1982; a direct manufacturer on a 20 acre site in Mansfield, Texas; more than 3,500 projects; permanent (pier and beam, slab-on-grade) and relocatable modular; SCIF buildings, disaster recovery, multi-family and student housing.
Contract vehicles on the site today: MBI, BuyBoard and TIPS.
The lead offer is no cost project planning and budgeting. It is the button on every page.
found: Semrush credits ramtechmodular.com with 2,084 organic keywords and about 2,343 visits a month, on an Authority Score of 24. Nearly nine visits in ten come from people who did not type the company name.
The site is 635 pages with an average page score of 49 of 100 (grade D); 424 of those pages score D or F. 13 findings, ranked on the Search page of this hub.
The home page title runs to 72 characters and its heading is the company's claim, which contains no term a buyer searches for. The home page has no form on it.
Every money page carries Article markup; none carries Service or FAQPage markup, and none shows a review.

Live searches from Mansfield put Ramtech first for six of seven local service searches, and absent from the top ten for the national head terms such as 'modular construction' and 'portable school buildings'.
All 13 AI crawlers tested are allowed in, but there is no llms.txt at the root of the site.
pitch.choose_intro: The words, the pages and the proof are identical in all three. What differs is the register. Open each one on your phone and tell us which feels like Ramtech.
choose_reasons: If a plain, procedural site is the argument
Clean: white ground, a humanist sans, hairline cards. Built for the facility manager, school business officer or procurement lead reading a page in order.
If a contemporary, confident look is the argument
Showcase: Plus Jakarta Sans, image-led and rounded. Shows the buildings first.
Press: warm paper and a serif. Reads like the company that has been building since 1982.
plan: Choose a direction. Confirm the project count and the contact for each form.
Copy review with Ramtech: the project profiles, the floor plans library, and which blog posts are worth keeping.
Build in HubSpot: theme, templates, every page, forms routed to the right person at the plant.
Review rounds, a permanent redirect for every URL that exists today, QA on the same gate this preview passed.
Launch with the baseline captured the day before.
Measure against the baseline and decide the first articles from the questions buyers ask.
confirm: Contact at Ramtech for this proposal. The brief names no one; Kelly Williams is shown on Ramtech's site as Vice President of Business Development.
Project count. The home page and the Ramtech story say more than 3,500, the brief says 3,500+, the Ramtech difference page says more than 4,000. Pages use 3,500.
Accent. #cd2122 is from the brief. It matches the roofs in the photographs; it was not checked against brand guidelines.
Logo. The colour logo (navy and maroon, 295 by 132 pixels) is taken from the live site, so the header is white. A vector file would sharpen it.

Photographs are Ramtech's own, 2017 to 2019, taken from the live site. The site does not caption which project is which, so alt text is descriptive only. A current set of finished buildings would help the hero.
Cities. Arlington is where Ramtech began in 1982 and Dallas-Fort Worth is the market; the site lists one address, in Mansfield. No Arlington or Dallas-Fort Worth office is shown.
No written testimonials are published (the video narrations are not quoted), so none appear.
The design team page names nobody, so no team section appears and no Person records are in the schema.
Mansfield coordinates (32.5632, -97.1417) are approximate and used only for schema markup.
